title and abstract.summary: This study measured the differences in functional traits among populations of the ant Pheidole nodus fragmented across various urban parks.

introduction.summary: This study examined workers of the ant species Pheidole nodus from urban parks in Nanchong city, China, to test for differences in how individuals from segregated populations fill morphological space (morphospace).

methods.summary: This study measured the foraging workers of the ant species Pheidole nodus across seven urban parks in Nanchong, China, to test the effects of environmental selection on ants actively foraging under urban habitat conditions. The study measured six continuous morphological traits for foraging worker ants of Pheidole nodus to identify key axes of morphological variation and then used these principal components to test environmental filter-strength and optimum-shift hypotheses across different parks. results.summary: This study measured the morphospace volume and centroid displacement of workers from the species Pheidole nodus collected across seven different parks in Nanchong City.

discussion.summary: The study measured the morphometric traits of populations of Pheidole nodus across seven urban parks to investigate variations in phenotypic diversity and trait optima in response to habitat conditions. The study measured the intra-specific morphological diversity of the population of Pheidole nodus workers at Xishan Park, finding that their morphological diversity was around average compared to the full meta-population sampled. This study measured the variance of functional morphology in foraging worker ants across different urban park populations to detect differences in morphospace.
